subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown cancel active runs and their managed exec child processes before the watchdog, or continue preserving background/yielded exec sessions unless an explicit restart or kill path is used?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve active/background work on normal shutdown, so changing it can stop long-running user work and needs maintainer policy rather than an automated bug patch.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Normal stop should reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed active run/exec scopes with documented exceptions for any background class maintainers preserve.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal stop from aborting active/background exec work and treat the report as a diagnostics or operator-documentation gap.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the session-wide exec list/kill contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines process ownership semantics.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Normal stop should reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed active run/exec scopes with documented exceptions for any background class maintainers preserve.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current path-history signal across gateway shutdown abort helpers, exec behavior, and process-supervisor adjacent work.
